chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by the oldest teaching substrate. Teaching purity is 0.912. The core teaching maps cosmic emanation processes onto immeasurable durations — a systematic cosmological teaching about the time-structure of divine evocations (Great Spirit, Mother of Life, First Man, five sons) and the parallel evil emanation from Matter. The six-fold enumeration (¶24-30) is a distinctive structural feature mapping temporal phases of cosmic history. The only significant later-layer intrusions are mild: (1) scattered first-person pedagogical address formulas ('Listen also to this, how I would teach you it'; 'which I have told you'), and (2) institutional vocabulary ('apostles and teachers') in ¶17-18, ¶30, ¶32 where the teaching about epistemic limits regarding eternity is framed through Manichaean institutional figures. No editorial bridge, no exhortation, no strong institutional material. The chapter is remarkably intact as substrate teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] a great ju[d/ge ...] now also a ti[me ...] that they sculpt[ed ...] he was revealed in the Father, the first established thing.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Very fragmentary. 'Sculpted' is emanation-process vocabulary. 'Revealed in the Father, the first established thing' is cosmic process language. Despite lacunae, the surviving vocabulary is substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: W[he]n [...] the two summonses that he called [...] the Mother of Life [...] a long duration in the first Father [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary. 'Two summonses,' 'Mother of Life,' 'long duration in the first Father' — all emanation-timing vocabulary. Substrate=13.64 supports classification.

paragraphs.core_text: For someone, if he might set a measure and rule [...] the earth {particles} and the {pebbles} of the mountains and [...] of the sea and the body of the firmaments. Should they be poured [...] the body of the four mountains and the three vessels that surround the universe; if they shall all be poured out [...] these fine {granules}.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cosmic geography: four mountains, three vessels surrounding the universe, firmaments. The measurement analogy (grains as comparison for immeasurable duration) maps cosmos→cosmos. Both sides internal to the system. Substrate=18.03.

paragraphs.core_text: The grains of the earth {particles} are measurable, [and those of] the [entire] universe. It is possible to count the {particles} of the earth each year [...] the sand grains of the entire universe; but the duration of the time that the Great Spirit spent in the Father, [the] first established thing, one will not be able to make a count of it!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Happen you know that' — pedagogical address formula (dialogue_frame=5.97 supports this).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core content is entirely cosmological: the Great Spirit's immeasurable duration in the Father. The opening address 'Happen you know that' is a mild frame formula wrapping substrate teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: He first sculpted her like this. He established her in his inner storehouses in quiet and silence. When [they had] need of her she was called and came forth of the Father [of Greatness]. She looked at all her aeons of light!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure emanation-process teaching: sculpting, inner storehouses, calling forth, aeons of light. 'In quiet and silence' is a distinctive substrate formula for pre-emanation state. Substrate=23.81, highest in the chapter.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, from the time when she was called to [...] go to [...] she gave [...] upon his [bod]y [...] all the aeons [...]; she also [...] all of them. This [is also the case] with the First Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: 'Once again' here is narrative continuation ('Once again, from the time when...'), NOT the dialogue frame formula 'Once again the enlightener speaks.' Continues emanation timing for the Mother of Life. Fragmentary but cosmological throughout.

paragraphs.core_text: This is how the Man spent a long time being anointed in the Mother, set fast in her inner storehouses [...]; from when the First Man went down to the contest, till the time when the [Statue (?) co]mes i[n ...] this time [...] he appeared [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'the extent of time that I have recounted to you—' — first-person address to audience, editorial pedagogical voice.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core is emanation-timing substrate: First Man anointed in the Mother, inner storehouses, descent to contest, Last Statue. The first-person aside ('I have recounted to you') is an editorial interpolation within otherwise pure substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, from when he was called and came forth, till the time when he [himse]lf called the five shining [gods] who are his sons; they themselves also spent a long time existing in their father! It is the time that occurred from the coming down of the First Man till the going up of the Last Statue. The five gods spent this much duration being anointed in the First Man. Yet, [at the] time when they were awaited, they were called and came forth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure emanation-timing substrate: five gods called from First Man, duration measured against cosmic descent-ascent cycle (First Man's coming down to Last Statue's going up). 'Being anointed' parallels ¶7. Substrate=16.67.

paragraphs.core_text: At the time when the Mother of Life was called from the Father of Greatness, when she expelled herself and came down by her own wish, from the heights of the Father to the earth, [she would spend thousands of] years and many ten thousands until she reached the earth. [Fo]r there is no measure nor rule to the heights of the Father. Rather, [just as] he had called her in his Great Spirit, so he set her upon [the] land of greatness through one of these three that are counted to the twelve hidden ones within the light veil, the ones [esta]blished after the [...] region of the south.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Listen also to this, how I would teach you it.' — first-person pedagogical frame formula.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Rich substrate content: Mother of Life's descent from Father of Greatness, cosmic geography (heights of the Father, land of greatness), structural reference to 'twelve hidden ones within the light veil' and 'region of the south.' This cosmic cartography is deep substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: [The] matter of the Mother [of L]ife is like this. When [the Father called her he established her in the place he pleased,] to establish her there as the instruction of the people that [...] many [...]; and she examined everywhere that [...] a blink of an eye, or like a [...] bird [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary. 'The instruction of the people' is ambiguous — could be editorial (community function) or substrate (cosmic role as guide). Given the overall substrate context and heavy lacunae, classified as substrate with uncertainty noted. 'A blink of an eye' describes cosmic instantaneity.

paragraphs.core_text: This also is lik[e ... the] Mother of Life in [...] whenever [...] cast her out [...] upon her to the place [...] him. He perfected her in his Great Spirit and set her in [the place he pl]eased, according to [his will].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary but cosmological throughout: Mother of Life, Great Spirit, establishing in the place according to will. Substrate=13.95.

paragraphs.core_text: [Th]is [also is how] they called the [five g]ods from the [Fi]rst Man. They were set before him, as he wished that [...]-ness [...] down, that they would rule in them [...] one another. He ordered and distributed them [...] the son. He stripped himself of them [...] and he [...] he girt and bound himself to [...] in a [...] of silence upon the border of the earth [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Five gods called from First Man. 'Stripped himself of them,' 'girt and bound himself' — preparation for descent. 'Silence upon the border of the earth' — cosmic geography. All mappings internal to system.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, he too, the First Man, spent a long period and [time] until he gave power to his sons; until he assu[m]ed them. After he came to wear them he stood fast in the heights between the borders. Again, he spent a duration and time like this, corresponding to such amount and measure as the raindrops and dew and falls of mist that come down in the universe. This is how he spent this duration also, standing between the borders, until the hour when he cast himself down to the contest!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate: First Man arming with his sons, standing in heights between borders, descent to contest. The duration-analogy (raindrops, dew, mist) maps cosmic time→natural phenomena — both sides within the cosmic system. 'Heights between the borders' is cosmic geography.

paragraphs.core_text: Whenever the Father of Greatn[e]ss called the Great Spirit and the First Man and the gods of the glorious one, who are provided to enable them to reveal him; at that very time [he] sculpted the Great Builder in the [land of] light, [and] the Living Spirit with the mighty and active gods who came [from] him. Also, at that time, he sculpted the [Amb]assador, with Jesus the Splendour and the Virgin of Light and the Pillar of Glory, and the gods who came from them. [All these the Father of Greatness sculpted at] a single time. They came forth of one another, one after one; the time when [...] and the work.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Key emanation teaching: simultaneous sculpting of all three evocations — Great Builder/Living Spirit, Ambassador/Jesus the Splendour/Virgin of Light/Pillar of Glory. 'Sculpted at a single time' and 'came forth of one another, one after one' describes the paradox of simultaneous-yet-sequential emanation. Highest substrate score (31.86). All entities are cosmic — 'Jesus the Splendour' is a cosmic figure, not the historical Jesus.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] from the time when the Darkness raised itself up to [...] essence of the light [...] these three emanations [...] from the will of the Father against the enemy [...] he has [...] Darkness [...] according to the will [...] the universe [...] in it [...] separate out [...] rest him in which way, and he rejoices [...] in his kingdom; until [the time when the face] of the Father will be unveiled over [all] the gods of glory, and all the rich ones of [...] the em[anations] who came forth against the enemy.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed '[...] to recount it to you [...]' — fragmentary first-person address to audience.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Heavily lacunose but cosmological throughout: Darkness rising, three emanations from Father's will, separation, Father's face unveiled. Darkness capitalized as personified agent. Only editorial intrusion is the tiny address fragment.

paragraphs.core_text: [From] that time when he sculpted these three [...] till the time when the Father would unveil his face, [and they] go in to his hidden storehouses, and he calls them [...] establishes each one of them to his place. There is no measure nor rule to this period until that time.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary of the cosmic time-span from sculpting to the Father's unveiling. 'Hidden storehouses,' 'no measure nor rule' — pure substrate vocabulary for immeasurable cosmic duration.

paragraphs.core_text: what has happened and what will happen; but before [...] they are sculpted in heaven there is no possibility [...] to proclaim about this beginning, because [...] for ever.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'It is possible for all [the teachers] and saviours and apostles of greatness, that they can speak and reveal about' and 'for any apostle and teacher' — institutional vocabulary (institutional=7.55). The Manichaean ecclesiastical figures are the vehicle for an older teaching about the unknowability of the eternal beginning.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The cosmological claim — that the beginning is eternal and beyond measure/speech — may be substrate, but the vehicle (apostles, teachers, saviours) is clearly institutional Manichaean. The underlying teaching about epistemic limits regarding eternity is preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: the time when all the fathers of light [go in to the hid]den (places) of the Father, and dwell [...] power in them to its [...] of God [...]; because it exists for ever. It is continuous till the aeons. It has no time to the end; but their establishment [...] eternal is their life [...] generation by generation.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Nor also is it possible for [all] the apostles and teachers to be able to speak and reveal [...]' — institutional framing (institutional=2.56). Same pattern as ¶17.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmological content: fathers of light returning to hidden places of the Father, eternal existence. 'It is continuous till the aeons. It has no time to the end' — substrate language about immeasurable duration. Institutional framing is the wrapper.

paragraphs.core_text: [If] a person shall ask [...] and about that eternal end [...] in the devastation [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Very fragmentary. 'Eternal end' and 'devastation' are cosmological. 'A person shall ask' is generic rather than institutional. Substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: this Matter, this thought of Death [...] came up to its storehouses. It has [...] in its five elements.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'However, [...] to enable him to recoun[t ...] who asks him [...] of the disciples [...] because [...] and he gives [...] about' and 'which I have told you; for [this] is the way that [...]' — pedagogical frame with first-person address and disciple reference. Heavy lacunae in the frame material.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The surviving substrate core names Matter and its five elements — the evil counterpart to the divine emanation. 'Thought of Death' is a personified attribute of Matter. Much lost to lacunae and frame material.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, it also [...] the period and the time that it spent, until it revealed itself to its elements, before it came to the trees. It spent a great period and a long time established [...] before it came up to the trees. It was [...] in the trees. It spent a long time and duration [...] existing in them, before it sculpted the fru[its ...] and sculpted the fruits.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Evil emanation parallel: Matter revealing itself to its elements, progressing to 'the trees,' sculpting fruits. This mirrors the divine emanation-timing but for the dark side. 'Trees' and 'fruits' are cosmic-correspondential, not botanical — they are the substrate of evil generation. Substrate=8.57.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, it spent a long [time] in the fruits. Not little is the period and the time that it spent existing in the fruits, before it sculpted [...] after a long time [...] the d[emon]s of its five worlds in various forms [can not (?) ] be measured [...] in p[erfec]tion of the fruits in the demons and fiends. They fell upon their earth and [...] were nourished. Not little is the period that they [spent in the wo]rlds, until they were nourished amongst [...] to make [...] that land which shines, and the great [King] who dwells there.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues evil emanation: from fruits to demons of five worlds, nourishment, the great King dwelling in the shining land. 'Five worlds' maps to the five-element system. 'The great King who dwells there' is the King of Darkness in his realm. All mappings internal to the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] at the time when he [...] its essence. It assumed [...] Matter [...] to the war [...] the Perfect Man. [From the time] when the war occurred [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed '[You] know that [...] that in [...]' — address formula to audience.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary. Transition from evil emanation timing to the war — Matter assuming essence, conflict with the Perfect Man. The war is the cosmic event, not a historical conflict.

paragraphs.core_text: [The first is ...] he came to be in some [...] when they ensnared a [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Begins the six-fold enumeration (¶24-30). Very fragmentary. Enumeration marker 'The first is' is substrate structure. 'Ensnared' suggests the cosmic entrapment.

paragraphs.core_text: [The second is ...] that he built [...] the universe was established. The zone [...] down until the time when it will be dissolved.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second item: cosmic construction — universe established, zone, dissolution. Maps cosmic phase → duration. Enumeration structure preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is the [...] the things and the universe will [...] from the time when they were established there, till the time when their end will be complete and their existence ceases [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third item: duration from establishment to completion of the universe's end. Pure cosmic timeline mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: [The fourth is the dissolution when they will dissolve the universe] there, and all things are destroyed. Obliteration reaches them in that great fire, [which will] burn them for fourteen hundred and sixty-eight years.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth item: cosmic dissolution by fire. The specific number — 1,468 years — is a distinctive substrate feature, a precise cosmic duration. This specificity marks archaic astronomical/cosmological calculation.

paragraphs.core_text: [The fift]h is the way that the Last Statue will be sculpted [from] the remnant of all things. The light separates out to its place, and goes up and rules in its kingdom. However, [the Da]rkness [...] and they take it in to the tomb [...] and they are bound with it in an eternal chain.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth item: Last Statue sculpted from remnant, light-dark final separation. 'Sculpted' links to the emanation vocabulary throughout the chapter. Darkness capitalized as personified agent bound in tomb. Substrate=14.29.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, from [the tim]e when this first war occurred, till the time of this chain [...] these five things [...] light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary of the five-fold enumeration: from the first war to the chaining. 'Now' here is a connective within the enumeration, not an editorial bridge marker — it summarizes the five cosmic phases just enumerated.

paragraphs.core_text: [The six]th: From the time when it stirred and raised itself up in its land, till the time of its chaining [...] However, before [...] from it out of the powers [...] and measure it; because it is eternal.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'it is possible for the apostles and the chosen and the teachers to speak and recount about it.' — institutional vocabulary (institutional=3.57). Same epistemic-limits pattern as ¶17-18.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Sixth item completes the enumeration. The cosmological frame — from Matter's stirring to its chaining, with the beginning being eternal — is substrate. The institutional identification of who can speak about it is the editorial addition. Enumeration marker preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: [From the time] when it will be taken in to the chaining and bound in the lump [...] to give to it. No person is able [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continuation of the chaining teaching. 'Bound in the lump' (bolos) is a technical cosmological term for the final imprisonment of Darkness. Substrate=14.81.

paragraphs.core_text: chaining is eternal [in the] lum[p ...] {}
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'the apostle and the teacher is enabled to [...]' — institutional vocabulary (institutional=11.76).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Very fragmentary. The cosmological claim — that the chaining in the lump is eternal — is substrate. The institutional framing (apostle, teacher) follows the same pattern as ¶17-18, ¶30. Highest institutional score in the chapter but the surviving cosmological content is minimal.
